newsitem.title: USA: Calif. unemployment rate drops to 6.3 pct - state.
newsitem.headline: Calif. unemployment rate drops to 6.3 pct - state.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped to 6.3 percent in May, down from 6.5 percent in April, the state said on Friday.
The May unemployment rate was the lowest since September 1990's 6.1 percent, the state Employment Development Department said in a report.
The state gained 41,400 jobs over the month.
A record-high 14.8 million people are now employed.
If the pace of job growth during the past six months continues through 1997, the state will add over 400,000 jobs during the year, according to the state report.
"California's economic expansion is continuing to break records," Gov. Pete Wilson said in a statement.
All industry sectors, except mining, posted job gains in May. Mining was unchanged.
Most of the job growth was in the services sector, up 18,800 jobs. Construction and wholesale trade added 3,800 and 2,600 jobs respectively.
The growth in manufacturing was primarily in the durable goods sector, while the gain in transportation and public utilities was mainly in trucking and warehousing.
